shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A patterned companionship poem answers the solitary toiler of 4:8: טוֹבִ֥ים הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם מִן הָאֶחָ֑ד (oshb:Eccl.4.9, byte tier) — “Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor.” (web:Eccl.4.9) — develops across three parallel illustrations (falling, warmth, and resistance) before closing, “…and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.” (web:Eccl.4.12).
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping this stretch as monologue_unit (the parent's operative default) was considered and rejected: unlike the surrounding first-person narration, 4:9-12 carries no first-person verb at all and runs a three-clause conditional construction with three distinct lead particles -- כִּ֣י אִם (oshb:Eccl.4.10, byte tier), גַּ֛ם אִם (oshb:Eccl.4.11, byte tier), and וְאִֽם (oshb:Eccl.4.12, byte tier) -- not an identical repeated opener, a formal structure closer to the book's other patterned poems than to sustained autobiographical prose. saying_cluster was also considered and rejected: the four verses form one continuous, grammatically dependent illustration series -- each of 4:10-4:12 illustrates 4:9's own 'two are better than one' thesis, closing on a single capping image at 4:12 -- rather than detachable, independently-standing sayings, so wisdom_poem's patterned-poem category fits better than a cluster of sayings.

next_row.boundary_rationale: The poor-youth-and-old-king narrative opens on a tov comparative, ט֛וֹב יֶ֥לֶד מִסְכֵּ֖ן וְחָכָ֑ם (oshb:Eccl.4.13, byte tier) — “Better is a poor and wise youth than an old and foolish king who doesn’t know how to receive admonition any more.” (web:Eccl.4.13) — and develops through the prison-to-throne reversal of 4:14 and the crowd-observation of 4:15 to its closing verdict, כִּֽי גַם זֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל וְרַעְי֥וֹן רֽוּחַ (oshb:Eccl.4.16, byte tier), “…Surely this also is vanity and a chasing after wind.” (web:Eccl.4.16). The referents of “the youth, the other, who succeeded him” (web:Eccl.4.15) are not named in the row’s own bytes, and this writer holds the identification of the two figures as genuinely open rather than resolving it by conjecture.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the narrative at 4:14 (the prison-to-throne reversal) from 4:15-16 (the crowd observation) was considered; it was rejected not because no marker separates them -- 4:15 opens with its own bare, asyndetic raiti-observation verb, רָאִ֨יתִי֙ (oshb:Eccl.4.15, byte tier), the same raiti device already registered for this row, and, being asyndetic rather than waw-prefixed, at least as strong a restart signal as the two waw-prefixed raiti instances (web:Eccl.3.22, web:Eccl.4.4) elsewhere in this monologue treated as genuine drivers -- but because that marker is grammatically overridden by referential dependency: 4:15's definite הַיֶּ֣לֶד הַשֵּׁנִ֔י (oshb:Eccl.4.15, byte tier), 'the second youth,' is anaphoric on the indefinite יֶ֥לֶד (oshb:Eccl.4.13, byte tier), 'a youth,' first introduced at 4:13, so the restart marker is present but overridden by that antecedent chain, and the closing verdict at 4:16 depends grammatically on the same narrated succession the whole unit describes.

next_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens on a bare imperative addressed to a worshipper, pointed “שְׁמֹ֣ר רגליך רַגְלְךָ֗” (web:Eccl.5.1 = oshb:Eccl.4.17, byte tier oshb:Eccl.4.17) -- the verb governs an unpointed ketiv object immediately corrected by its pointed qere within the same clause (single-witness WLC; check pmarks kq before slicing this seam verse). WEB renders the clause “Guard your steps when you go to God’s house” (web:Eccl.5.1). Five occurrences of the negative particle “אַל” (oshb:Eccl.5.1, byte tier; pointed with patach, not the segol-pointed homograph preposition of the same bare consonants) open successive clauses at oshb:Eccl.5.1 (twice, both bare tokens), oshb:Eccl.5.3, and oshb:Eccl.5.5 (twice, the second carrying the ו-prefix, “וְאַל”) -- a negative-imperative chain running web:Eccl.5.2-Eccl.5.6 = oshb:Eccl.5.1-Eccl.5.5 that holds the unit together as one address on cultic and verbal conduct (count: 5 tokens across 3 verses, hand-swept from the cited spans). The same patach-pointed particle recurs once more immediately past this row’s own close, “אַל תִּתְמַ֖הּ עַל הַחֵ֑פֶץ” (oshb:Eccl.5.7, byte tier), so the chain is disclosed as continuing rather than terminating cleanly at this row’s own boundary; the root חפץ links this row’s own “אֵ֥ין חֵ֖פֶץ” (oshb:Eccl.5.3, byte tier) to that verse’s own חפץ token, and the root שמר links this row’s opening “שְׁמֹ֣ר” (oshb:Eccl.4.17, byte tier) to that verse’s own “שֹׁמֵ֔ר” (oshb:Eccl.5.7, byte tier) -- both disclosed here as texture, not as this row’s boundary driver. The address closes on a motto rather than a new topic: “כִּ֥י אֶת הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים יְרָֽא” (oshb:Eccl.5.6, byte tier), “you must fear God” (web:Eccl.5.7), which answers the opening reverence-in-the-house frame and remains the row’s own actual, sufficient boundary driver, marking the close before the discourse pivots to a different register at web:Eccl.5.8.
